news.title: FIFA president Gianni Infantino gets support from Malawi amid pressure
news.lede: Malawi's historic qualification for the 2027 Women's World Cup is a reflection of the increased investment in African football during Gianni Infantino's tenure as FIFA president, according to Malawi Football Association president Fleetwood Haiya.Speaking to Reuters, Haiya said the progress made under Infantino's leadership was a key reason he continues to back the FIFA chief. Malawi have emerged as one of the biggest surprises at the ongoing Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. Their run to the semi-finals has secured their place at next year's Women's World Cup, marking a significant milestone for the country's women's football team."

news.title: Who is Omar Artan? UEFA Super Cup ref who was refused entry to USA in World Cup chaos
news.lede: Omar Artan profile: Omar Abdulkadir Artan is a 34-year-old professional football referee from Somalia who has steadily built a strong reputation over the past few years. His profile rose significantly when he was named the 2025 Confederation of African Football (CAF) Men's Referee of the Year, an award he received shortly after becoming the first Somali to oversee a CAF Champions League final. Background : His consistent performance on the continent led to him being selected by FIFA as a match official for the 2026 World Cup, representing a major historic achievement for his nation. He was set to become the very first referee from Somalia to officiate at a World Cup finals tournament, a milestone that brought immense pride to the Somali sporting community and resulted in a warm reception upon his recent return to Mogadishu.

news.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
news.lede: Messi’s father, ⁠Jorge, died last week at age of 68. Argentinian suggests he may not play on much longer. Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father. Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Malawi FA chief backs Infantino, credits FIFA investment for World Cup breakthrough
news.lede: RABAT, Aug 12 (Reuters) - Malawi's qualification for the ⁠2027 Women's World Cup is a result of investment in African football made by FIFA under President Gianni Infantino and why he will ⁠likely enjoy the support of the continent, the country's football association President Fleetwood Haiya told Reuters. Malawi have been the surprise package of ‌the ongoing Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco, and earned their World Cup berth by reaching the semi-finals. Haiya credits Infantino's focus on investing in African football during his tenure, and what he perceives as an attempt to level the playing field, as the reason why he will continue to support the beleaguered FIFA president.

news.title: Messi drops massive retirement hint in emotional tribute to father
news.lede: Lionel Messi has shared a tribute to his late father, Jorge, on social media, opening up about how difficult it was to lead Argentina to the World Cup final and expressing uncertainty about whether he will continue playing football. “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you,” the post said in Spanish, shared on the footballer’s Instagram on Wednesday. Argentina’s Lionel Messi reacts to the team’s loss in the World Cup final. “I don’t know how to keep going.

news.title: Dad, I Still Can't Believe You're Gone: Messi's Heartbreaking Goodbye
news.lede: Lionel Messi has spent most of his life finding ways to express himself with a football. On Wednesday, he was searching for words to say goodbye to the man who had been there almost from the first kick. Jorge Messi, Lionel Messi's father, longtime agent, adviser and one of the central figures in his extraordinary football journey, died at a clinic in Rosario after a prolonged illness. For Messi, the grief is intertwined with one final football memory: the 2026 World Cup.

news.title: De Zerbi: ‘Tonali a leader at Tottenham, can learn from Argentina at 2026 World Cup’
news.lede: Roberto De Zerbi explains why Sandro Tonali can be ‘a leader’ at his new Tottenham Hotspur project, bringing Italian techniques to the Premier League, and learning from Argentina at the World Cup. The Italian tactician is only 47 years old, but has already worked in Italy, Ukraine, France and England, taking over the Spurs job in March 2026. He had to drag them out of the relegation zone in the final weeks of the campaign, and is now determined to start afresh in the Premier League with an expensive transfer strategy. That includes the arrival of fellow Italian Tonali, who cost over €115m to buy from Newcastle United, and it’s reported the coach helped convince him to choose them ahead of Manchester City or Arsenal.

news.title: Messi says not certain to play ‘much longer’ after father’s death
news.lede: Argentina superstar and inspiration behind his country’s 2022 World Cup victory, Lionel Messi, said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) he has “serious doubts” about continuing to play football for “much longer” after the death of his father Jorge Messi. “I don’t know what I’ll do without you, I don’t know how to go on. I just played football, and now I have serious doubts about continuing to do so for much longer,” Messi, 39, wrote in a message on social media after his father, who was also his agent, died last week aged 68. In the message, Messi, whose contract with Major League Soccer outfit Inter Miami runs till the end of the 2028 season, reflected on the final months of his father’s life, which coincided with the 2026 World Cup.
